key_insight: Differentiable foundation models enable joint optimization of crystal composition and structure to design semiconductors with band gaps targeted for photovoltaic absorption.
engineering_relevance: The approach could accelerate solar-absorber discovery by optimizing band gaps while penalizing energetically unfavorable crystal designs.
method: DEFEAT extends pretrained EquiformerV3 to continuous species weights and site occupancies without retraining on fractional data.
Property gradients and a learned energy penalty jointly update composition, atom count, atomic positions, and lattice vectors.
SCAN calculations assess candidate band gaps and stability relative to the DFT convex hull.
evidence_signal: SCAN calculations confirmed ten novel crystal structures with band gaps within 20% of a 1.34 eV target on their respective raw or empirically corrected scales, all within 70 meV/atom of the DFT hull.
watch_item: Training-functional band-gap bias propagates into designs unless corrected in the objective; target gaps alone do not establish solar-cell performance.
paper_title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
